newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans fall for 20th month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans fall for 20th month.

text.p: The value of loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 14.96 percent in December 1996 from a year earlier, the central bank said on Tuesday.
December was the 20th consecutive month of declines. It followed a 16.35 percent year-on-year fall in November.
Loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses were down 3.86 percent to T$2.891 trillion in December from a year ago, the central bank said.
December's overall decline was the ninth monthly fall in 10 years -- and all were in 1996.

Lending fell 0.35 percent in January, 0.80 percent in May, 1.1 percent in June, 2.21 percent in July, 4.95 percent in August, 9.21 percent in September, 5.41 percent in October, and 5.02 percent in November.
Central bank officials had attributed the flat-to-negative growth to a persistent overall slowing in the economy.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has seen deep recession since the local real estate market peaked in 1989.
